The drawing shows a 1H-indazole ring with the NH group attached at position 5 of the benzo ring.

**Indazole.** The pyrazole ring carries N at the top (N=CH) and HN at the left, fused to the benzene ring. The NH nitrogen is bonded to C7a, and C3 is the CH double-bonded to N2.

**Substituent.** The indazole C5 is bonded to an NH. That nitrogen is bonded to a CH, which carries a CO2Et group (C(=O)OEt) and a CH2. The CH2 leads to C(=O)O-tBu.

**Position check.** The benzene ring atoms are C3a (top right, bonded to C3), C4 (top, CH), C5 (right, bearing the NH), C6, C7 and C7a. C3a is at the upper-right of the fusion and C4 lies below it. The substituent sits on the carbon at the lower right, which is two bonds from C3a, so it is C5. This is consistent with the 5-aminoindazole reading.

**SMILES.** Written from the NH-bearing carbon:
CCOC(=O)C(CC(=O)OC(C)(C)C)Nc1ccc2[nH]ncc2c1

Ring check: c1 (C5), c (C6), c (C7), c2 (C7a) with [nH] attached, then n (N2), c (C3), c2 (C3a), and c1 (C4) closing back to C5. This matches the drawing.

The stereocentre is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is given.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)C(CC(=O)OC(C)(C)C)Nc1ccc2[nH]ncc2c1
